content.hypothesis: Navigating directly to the semantically most likely container for a perishable food item (the fridge) before scanning other receptacles reduces total search steps compared to following the arbitrary spatial order of the initial observation list.
content.realization_pattern: Semantic-prior-first traversal: select the single most probable container type based on object properties, then fall back to standard scan.
content.scope: ALFWorld pick-and-place tasks where the target object is a food item (e.g., egg) and the room contains both high-probability semantic containers (fridge) and low-probability open surfaces, testing if semantic prioritization outperforms spatial listing order.

content.hypothesis: Prioritizing inspection of open surfaces (countertops, shelves) before closed storage units (fridge, cabinets) reduces total action steps for locating perishable food items compared to semantic-priority search (checking fridge first), by avoiding the overhead of opening/closing containers when the item is likely on an accessible surface.
content.realization_pattern: Open-surface-first traversal: exhaustively check all non-container receptacles before initiating container-opening actions.
content.scope: ALFWorld kitchen tasks where the target is a perishable food item (e.g., egg) and the room contains both open surfaces and closed storage units.

content.hypothesis: Prioritizing inspection of open surfaces before checking the semantically likely but costly-to-open fridge reduces total action steps for locating perishable food items compared to semantic-priority search.
content.realization_pattern: Open-surface-first traversal: exhaustively check all non-container receptacles before initiating container-opening actions.
content.scope: ALFWorld kitchen tasks where the target is a perishable food item (e.g., egg) and the environment contains mixed open surfaces (countertops, shelves) and closed storage units (fridge, cabinets).
